name: Howard Eaton
role: Bad Lands cattleman who called the first stockmen's meeting
bio: Howard Eaton was one of the most frequently named cattlemen in the Cow Boy, signing the February 1884 notices that called Bad Lands stockmen together for a meeting. That spring the paper reported that two visiting lumbermen, G. F. Randall and A. J. Rich, would put 1,000 head on the range in his charge, and in June 1884 he and Lloyd Roberts drove in a thousand head for the Badger cattle company. He spent the winter of 1884-85 on an eastern trip for treatment of his leg, received three carloads of bulls in June 1885, and regularly hosted eastern visitors from Pittsburgh and Boston for hunting in the Bad Lands. In February 1886 he obtained a lawyer's opinion that the Stark County tax levied on the area was unconstitutional, and that spring he brought a Bismarck dentist to Medora for a week. In October 1886 he sold three cars of cattle in St. Paul, and in November the new Billings County commissioners paid him for election work in the county's organization.
